selection_rationale.adversarial-document-reviewer: significant paginated reactive-source architecture and explicit alternatives

findings.title: AE5 incorrectly claims R5 coverage
findings.why_it_matters: The acceptance-example coverage map says the reconnect scenario verifies the SplitRequired publication rule, but its setup and outcome contain no split result. Readers could treat R5 as acceptance-covered even though this example cannot exercise it.
findings.suggested_fix: Change AE5's Covers line from R5, R9, R10, R12 to R9, R10, R12.
evidence: AE5 had Covers: R5, R9, R10, R12.
AE5 only describes reconnect and rebuild.

findings.title: Predefine the decision rule
findings.why_it_matters: Without a predetermined threshold for update-work reduction and acceptable bootstrap/subscription cost, the same measurements can be interpreted after the fact as support, rejection, or an inconclusive result, leaving the Direction 1b decision vulnerable to confirmation bias.
findings.suggested_fix: Before planning, define the quantitative comparison rule: the workload matrix, the metric(s) that establish affected-page-size rather than loaded-window scaling, and the maximum acceptable bootstrap, retained-state, and live-subscription trade-off for a proceed, reject, or narrowly scoped result.
evidence: Success Criteria classifies measurements as supported, disproved, or inconclusive.
Outstanding Questions asks what trade-off constitutes proceed, reject, or narrowly scoped.

residual_risks: Global merge/order or downstream publication may remain loaded-window scale even if page delivery is localized.
deferred_questions: Which quantitative threshold determines whether the trade-off justifies proceeding?
